newsitem.title: IRAQ: Syrian clothing firms hold trade fair in Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Syrian clothing firms hold trade fair in Iraq.

text.p: Syrian clothing companies are exhibiting in Baghdad in a bid to sell Iraq goods under its oil-for-food deal with the United Nations, Iraqi newspapers said on Tuesday.
"Representatives of 24 Syrian firms specialising in ready-made clothes started a three-day show of their products yesterday," the official al-Qadissiya said.
It quoted a member of the Syrian businessmen's council, Fawaz al-Baroodi, as saying Syrian firms would also take part on a much bigger scale in the annual Baghdad trade fair in November.

The oil deal, which took effect last December, allows Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to buy urgent needs for Iraqis, suffering from U.N. sanctions imposed for Baghdad's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
Iraq and Syria decided last month to reopen their borders for trade, closed since the beginning of the 1980s when ties were cut because Damascus sided with Iran in the 1980-88 Iraq-Iran war.
Since then the two Arab countries, ruled by rival factions of the Baath party, have been exchanging economic teams.

Iraq's Trade Minister Mohammed Mehdi Saleh said last week while opening a Syrian medical fair in Baghdad that Iraq had signed contracts worth $20 million with Syria to supply wheat, beans, soap and detergents under the oil deal.
The United Nations approved on Friday a location on the Iraqi-Syrian border as a new entry point for goods bought by Baghdad under the oil pact.
